job.title: Counsellor
job.description:
Pathway Talent is recruiting on behalf of New Horizons Enterprises Ltd for an experienced Carer Counsellor to join the Carer Gateway team.

This role provides an opportunity to support unpaid carers experiencing emotional, psychological and relationship challenges associated with their caring responsibilities. Through short-term therapeutic interventions, you will help carers strengthen their wellbeing, resilience, coping strategies and confidence.

About the Role
 As a Carer Counsellor, you will provide professional, evidence-informed counselling within the Carer Gateway service model.

You will work closely with Carer Navigators, Coaches, multidisciplinary colleagues and external services to ensure carers receive responsive, coordinated and appropriate support. Services may be delivered face-to-face, by telephone and through secure digital platforms.

Your key responsibilities will include:

  • Providing evidence-informed counselling to carers experiencing emotional, psychological and relationship challenges associated with their caring role.
  • Completing psychosocial assessments, formulation and intervention planning.
  • Providing individual, family and group counselling in line with program guidelines.
  • Applying strengths-based, solution-focused, grief and loss, CBT-informed, ACT-informed and trauma-informed approaches where clinically appropriate.
  • Supporting carers to strengthen coping skills, emotional wellbeing, resilience, self-care and confidence.
  • Undertaking risk assessments relating to suicide, self-harm, domestic and family violence, neglect, abuse and other safeguarding concerns.
  • Developing safety plans and escalating identified risks appropriately.
  • Supporting carers to access additional services such as advocacy, aged care, mental health, disability, peer support, coaching and community services.
  • Maintaining accurate and timely clinical records and treatment documentation.
  • Participating in clinical supervision, reflective practice, service development and continuous improvement activities.

About You
 You will bring a professional, compassionate and person-centred approach, together with the clinical capability to support carers experiencing a range of complex circumstances.

To be successful, you will have:

  • A tertiary qualification in Counselling, Psychology, Social Work, Psychotherapy or another relevant behavioural health discipline, with qualifications recognised in Australia.
  • Current accreditation or eligibility for membership with an appropriate Australian professional association, such as the Australian Counselling Association (ACA), Psychotherapy and Counselling Federation of Australia (PACFA), or Australian Association of Social Workers (AASW).
  • A minimum of three years’ work experience in Australia.
  • Demonstrated experience delivering therapeutic counselling services, including conducting needs assessments and providing individual counselling sessions.
  • Experience undertaking psychosocial and risk assessments and responding appropriately to identified needs and risks.
  • Demonstrated experience in, and the ability to provide, Rogerian/person-centred and/or Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT), or similar therapeutic approaches.
  • Sound knowledge and practical understanding of grief and loss, trauma-informed practice, family systems and strengths-based approaches.
  • A strong understanding of confidentiality, privacy, professional boundaries and ethical practice requirements.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to effectively engage with clients and build professional, respectful relationships.
  • The ability to work autonomously, manage competing priorities and exercise sound professional judgement, while also working collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team.
  • Strong clinical documentation, record-keeping and computer literacy skills, including the ability to maintain accurate and timely client records.
  • Current professional indemnity insurance appropriate to the relevant professional discipline.

Highly Regarded
It would be advantageous if you also have:

  • Experience supporting carers, families or people affected by disability, mental illness, chronic illness or ageing.
  • Knowledge of Carer Gateway, My Aged Care, disability and community service systems.
  • Experience facilitating therapeutic or psychoeducational groups.
  • An understanding of culturally responsive and trauma-informed practice.
  • Experience working with First Nations communities and culturally diverse populations.

Pre-Employment Requirements
The position description identifies requirements including:

  • National Criminal History Check.
  • Working with Children Check and NDIS Worker Screening Check where required by the contract, duties or service setting.
  • Current unrestricted Australian driver's licence.
  • Access to suitable transport for work-related travel.
  • Evidence of the right to work in Australia.
  • Completion of relevant mandatory and role-specific training.

A Safe and Inclusive Workplace
Pathway Talent has a zero-tolerance approach to abuse, neglect and harm and is committed to safeguarding the wellbeing of children, young people, people with disability and the communities we serve.

In line with this commitment, all appointments are subject to the successful completion of relevant pre-employment and safeguarding checks, including background screening, qualification and registration verification, and any role-specific compliance requirements.

Diversity & Inclusion
Pathway Talent is committed to supporting inclusive, diverse and culturally safe workplaces.

We strongly encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people with disability, members of the LGBTQIA+ community, and people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds.

Ready to Make an Impact?
If you’re an experienced counselling professional who is passionate about supporting carers and delivering high-quality, person-centred therapeutic support, we’d love to hear from you.

This is an opportunity to use your professional expertise to help unpaid carers strengthen their wellbeing, resilience and capacity to sustain their caring role.

Please note that only shortlisted applicants will be contacted.

job.title: Mental Health Service Manager
job.description:
Pathway Talent is proud to be recruiting on behalf of New Horizons Enterprises Ltd for an experienced Mental Health Service Manager to lead its CLS program within the Blacktown region.

New Horizons is a diverse not-for-profit organisation supporting people across mental health, disability, aged care and other community services. With wellbeing at the heart of its work, New Horizons is focused on empowering people to achieve their individual goals and aspirations.

This is an opportunity for an experienced mental health leader to combine people leadership, practice development and service improvement while supporting the delivery of high-quality, person-centred services.

About the Role
As the Mental Health Service Manager, you will provide leadership and accountability across the CLS program, ensuring consumers receive safe, effective and recovery-oriented support.

You will provide leadership to the multidisciplinary team, including the Practice Lead and frontline staff, building an engaged, capable and high-performing workforce while ensuring service delivery meets CLS program requirements, contractual obligations and organisational standards.

A key focus of the role will be ensuring the consistent implementation and fidelity of the CLS model of practice, supporting high-quality, recovery-oriented and person-centred service delivery.

You will also promote lived experience-informed practice, consumer participation and co-design, ensuring consumer perspectives contribute meaningfully to service delivery, continuous improvement and service development.

The position sits within the LHD Level CLS program, reports to the General Manager and is classified at SCHADS Level 6.1.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Lead the delivery of high-quality, evidence-based, trauma-informed and recovery-oriented mental health services.
  • Lead, support and develop the multidisciplinary team, including the Practice Lead and frontline team members.
  • Ensure consistent implementation and fidelity to the CLS model of practice across service delivery.
  • Promote lived experience-informed practice, consumer participation and co-design across service delivery and continuous improvement.
  • Strengthen supervision, coaching, onboarding and professional development across the team.
  • Build workforce capability and identify opportunities for training and development.
  • Maintain oversight of consumer service delivery, risk management and safeguarding.
  • Support effective care planning in partnership with consumers, clinicians and the broader multidisciplinary team.
  • Build strong working relationships with Local Health District mental health clinicians, housing providers, families and carers.
  • Monitor service performance, CLS KPIs, outcomes and quality.
  • Use service data to identify trends, risks and opportunities for improvement.
  • Drive continuous improvement and contribute to service development and innovation, incorporating consumer perspectives and feedback.
  • Ensure compliance with organisational policies, CLS guidelines, contractual obligations and relevant legislation.

About You
You're an experienced mental health professional and people leader who can balance quality service delivery with team development, stakeholder engagement and operational accountability.
You will bring:

  • At least a Certificate IV in Mental Health or equivalent, or other tertiary qualifications in a relevant health-related discipline.
  • At least 2 years' experience leading a mental health service.
  • Strong understanding of the CLS model of practice and the delivery of community-based mental health support. Experience within CLS or comparable programs, such as HASI+ or CLS-R, will be highly regarded.
  • Comprehensive knowledge of person-centred and recovery-oriented care, trauma-informed practice and cultural competence.
  • A commitment to lived experience-informed practice, consumer participation and co-design.
  • Strong communication, coaching and conflict-resolution skills.
  • The ability to adapt your communication style to effectively engage with a diverse range of people.
  • Willingness to undertake supervision training.

Desirable

  • Experience mentoring staff.
  • Familiarity with the NSW Mental Health Act.
  • Lived experience of mental health challenges, or carer experience, with a willingness to bring this perspective to practice leadership.

Checks and Certifications
The successful applicant must hold, or be willing and eligible to obtain prior to commencement:

  • NDIS Worker Check
  • National Police Check
  • Working with Children Check
  • Full Australian working rights
  • Current valid NSW Driver's Licence

A Safe and Inclusive Workplace
Pathway Talent has a zero-tolerance approach to abuse, neglect and harm and is committed to safeguarding the wellbeing of children, young people, people with disability and the communities we serve.

In line with this commitment, all appointments are subject to the successful completion of relevant pre-employment and safeguarding checks, including background screening, qualification and registration verification, and any role-specific compliance requirements.

Diversity & Inclusion
Pathway Talent is committed to supporting inclusive, diverse and culturally safe workplaces.

We strongly encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people with disability, members of the LGBTQIA+ community, and people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds.

Ready to Make an Impact?
If you're an experienced mental health leader with a strong understanding of community-based mental health service delivery and the CLS model, and a passion for developing people, strengthening practice quality and improving outcomes for consumers, we'd love to hear from you.

Please note that only shortlisted applicants will be contacted.

job.title: Youth Suicide Prevention Peer Worker
job.description:
Make a meaningful difference

Pathway Talent is recruiting on behalf of a well-established for-purpose organisation with more than 55 years of experience supporting individuals, families and communities. We are seeking a Youth Suicide Prevention Peer Worker to join an innovative psychosocial support program that supports children and young people up to 25 years of age who have lived experience of suicide, suicidality and self-harm.

Grounded in lived experience and peer support, this program provides a safe and supportive environment where young people can connect, build resilience and work towards recovery. We're looking for someone with lived experience who is passionate about walking alongside young people and their support networks, helping them navigate emotional or mental distress and create positive pathways forward.

About the role
Using your own lived experience of recovery, you'll provide tailored, lived experience-driven psychosocial support that meets each young person where they are. Your work will focus on enhancing wellbeing, building resilience and helping young people recover from adversity.

What you'll do

  • Build and maintain strong, trusting relationships with children and young people (CYP), their families and carers, team members and stakeholders.
  • Work collaboratively to assess support needs and deliver supports in line with relevant practice, quality frameworks and standards.
  • Draw on recovery-oriented, trauma-informed and strengths-based practice in all interactions.
  • Co-develop, implement and review realistic, evidence-based support plans with young people, their families and the Clinical Lead.
  • Use your personal lived experience of a suicidal crisis and/or distress to provide peer support meaningfully and purposefully.
  • Participate in intake and review meetings, and contribute to safety planning and risk assessment.
  • Maintain accurate, timely records and support the Clinical Lead with reporting obligations.
  • Contribute to service co-design, Youth Advisory Groups and continuous improvement, working closely with the Lived Experience Lead and other Peer Workers.

What you'll bring

  • Lived experience of ongoing recovery from suicidality, emotional or mental distress, this is essential to the role.
  • Formal peer support training (e.g. Certificate IV in Mental Health or Mental Health Peer Work), or a willingness to undertake it.
  • Experience providing peer-based psychosocial support to children and/or young people in a mental health or similar setting, including contributing to risk assessments and safety plans.
  • Clear, compassionate communication and strong active-listening skills.
  • Proven capacity to apply trauma-informed and recovery-oriented principles with care, respect and a focus on safety.
  • The ability to work within multidisciplinary teams and engage with external stakeholders.
  • Strong organisational and documentation skills.
  • Knowledge of relevant legislation, including child protection and mandatory reporting obligations.

Checks and certifications
The successful applicant must hold, or be willing and eligible to obtain before commencing:

  • NDIS Worker Check
  • National Police Check
  • Working with Children Check
  • Full Australian working rights

job.title: General Practitioners | Headspace Sydney
job.description:
Headspace is inviting General Practitioners to register their interest in joining our team across Sydney. Whether you're ready to start soon or simply exploring what a different way of practising might look like, we'd welcome a conversation.

A different way to practise

As a GP with Headspace, you'll work alongside psychologists, mental health clinicians, social workers, and allied health professionals to deliver integrated care to young people aged 12-25.

Unlike traditional general practice, you'll have the time to build meaningful therapeutic relationships. Longer consultations allow you to undertake thorough assessments, provide genuinely person-centred care, and focus on what matters most: supporting young people to achieve better health and wellbeing outcomes without the volume and administrative burden often associated with standard practice.

What's on offer

  • Attractive guaranteed hourly rate
  • Flexible working arrangements with your choice of preferred days
  • Longer consultations and the time to provide quality care
  • Dedicated administration time, supported by an experienced administration team
  • A collaborative and genuinely multidisciplinary team environment
  • The opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of young people

With opportunities across our Sydney centres, you'll have the flexibility to work within diverse communities at Ashfield, Chatswood and Brookvale.

Our centres support culturally and linguistically diverse communities, and we warmly welcome expressions of interest from GPs from culturally and linguistically diverse (CALD) backgrounds.
